newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of PPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of PPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in lacklustre trade, dealers said on Friday.

They said most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. February producer price index (PPI), January business inventories and February industrial production/capacity utilisation data.
The producer price index for February is forecast to show a decline of 0.1 percent compared with a 0.3 percent fall reported in January.
January business inventories are expected to show an increase of 0.2 percent against December's 0.1 percent fall.
Industrial production for February is expected to be unchanged from January's 0.5 percent increase and capacity utilisation for February is expected to rise to 83.5 percent versus 83.3 percent.

"Rates were quiet and featureless in the morning on some position adjustments. All eyes are on tonight's release of the PPI, business inventories, industrial production and capacity utilisation data," a local dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the weekend," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend was unchanged from Thursday's 5-5/16 5-3/16 percent.
Monday/Tuesday rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent but week-fixed eased 1/16 point to 5-3/8 5-1/4 percent.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-7/16 5-5/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-9/16 5-7/16, nine-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months unchanged at 6 5-7/8 percent.
